bib.title: Emergent Coordination in Multi-Agent Language Models

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Emergent Coordination in Multi-Agent Language Models", Christoph Riedl (Northeastern). arXiv 2510.05174v4 (cs.MA, 28 Apr 2026). The PDF header reads "Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026". Code: github.com/riedlc/AI-GBS.
COVERAGE: All 87,519 chars read, including the appendices (A.1-A.14, Table A2) and the limitations paragraph. References were skimmed. The extraction is clean. I did not run the figure-caption script, so the figure captions below come from the extracted text.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Claim: Prompting alone moves a multi-agent group from an aggregate toward an integrated collective. Persona prompts give stable identity-linked differentiation. Persona plus a "think about what others might do" (ToM) prompt adds goal-directed complementarity.
  number: none (headline qualitative result)
  setup: GPT-4.1 (2025-04-14), N=10 agents, T=1, no inter-agent communication, 200 groups per condition (600 total), one guessing task.
  quote: "Combining personas with an instruction to "think about what other agents might do" shows identity-linked differentiation and goal-directed complementarity across agents."
  where: abstract
- Claim: Raw success rate did not differ across the three conditions, so the steering shows in coordination structure and not in the success rate.
  number: none ("ns")
  setup: same as above
  quote: "Overall success rate is not significantly different across the interventions (Figure 2a)."
  where: Sec 3.2, p.6
- Claim: Only the ToM condition shows significant triplet mutual information (I3) and Total Stability. Plain and Persona sit near zero, which the paper reads as an uncoordinated "gaseous" state.
  number: ToM I3 p = 3.5e-14; Plain p = 0.974; Persona p = 0.846. Total Stability p = 2.9e-14 for ToM.
  setup: GPT-4.1, N=10, time-trend demeaned, bias-corrected, Wilcoxon test
  quote: "ToM shows significant positive mutual information (p= 3.5×10 −14), collapsing the group's behavior into a predictable macro-state"
  where: Sec 4.2, p.7
- Claim: ToM stability comes from dense pairwise alignment to the shared group signal ("mean field"), not from irreducible triplet synergy. G3 is about 0 in Persona and ToM. The authors call this "robust but informationally redundant".
  number: none
  quote: "the ToM prompt creates a deep basin of attraction where agents converge on a shared schematic (or Schelling point), making the collective state robust but informationally redundant."
  where: p.7
- Claim: Agent differentiation rises Plain < Persona < ToM. In Plain, differentiation is only noise and drift. Persona and ToM add stable identity-linked roles.
  number: none in text (Fig 3d only; Table A2 gives other-model percentages)
  quote: "There is substantially more differentiation among agents in the Persona condition, and even more in the ToM condition."
  where: p.8
- Claim: Emergence capacity exists in all conditions, including the plain control. Under the strict functional-null test, only ToM shows synergy.
  number: Practical criterion BC: Plain p = 1.5e-16, Persona p = 6.6e-7, ToM p = 0.02. Emergence capacity BC for ToM: p = 0.099 (marginal).
  setup: GPT-4.1, N=10, 2-bin quantile binning. 3.5% of individual groups had p<0.05 on the practical criterion.
  quote: "The bias-corrected estimates are well above 0 in all conditions (Plain: p= 1.5×10 −16; Persona: p= 6.6×10 −7; ToM: p= 0.02)."
  where: Sec 4.1, p.6
- Claim: Performance improves only when synergy and redundancy are both present. Either one alone does not predict success.
  number: interaction β = 0.24, p = 0.014; 27% amplification on the log-odds scale. Mediation ACME = 0.034, p = 0.053 (marginal).
  setup: Synergy and redundancy measured over the first 10 rounds only. IPW corrects for censoring (about 23% of runs end before round 10). Controls for task difficulty.
  quote: "when both are present, performance improves significantly (significant interaction with β= 0.24; p= 0.014)."
  where: Sec 4.3, p.8; A.11
- Claim: The ToM effect on performance runs through synergy, but only marginally.
  number: ACME = 0.034, 95% CI [-0.000, 0.07], p = 0.053
  quote: "the ToM treatment causally increases performance indirectly by increasing synergy (ACME= 0.034 [95%CI: −0.000−0.07], p= 0.053)."
  where: p.9
- Claim: Other models: success rates on a 10-agent group, 100 replications per condition per model, T=1. Persona and ToM beat Plain for the stronger models, with an exception for Qwen3 ToM. Llama-8B mostly fails.
  number: Table A2 success (Plain / Persona / ToM): Llama-8B 11% / 14% / 5.5%; Llama-70B 53% / 59% / 61%; Gemini 2.0 Flash 60% / 75% / 71%; Qwen3-235B 51% / 71% / 58%. Differentiation for Llama-8B ToM is 80%, below its Persona 92%.
  quote: "SuccessP lain 11% 53% 60% 51% / SuccessP ersona 14% 59% 75% 71% / SuccessT oM 5.5% 61% 71% 58%"
  where: Table A2, p.23
- Claim: Reasoning model Qwen3 shows "paralysis under coordination ambiguity", meaning looping chain-of-thought that does not terminate. One extra prompt line mitigates it.
  number: none
  quote: "If you find yourself re-evaluating your guess more than once, repeat your last guess."
  where: A.13, p.22
- Claim: Group size hurts and temperature helps. Each extra member lowers the odds of success. Higher temperature raises them.
  number: group size OR = 0.92 per member (p<1e-16); temperature OR = 1.50 per unit (p<1e-7)
  setup: GPT-4.1, group size 3-15, T 0-1 in 0.1 steps, 50 groups per cell, 7,150 runs
  quote: "each additional group member decreased the odds of success by roughly 8% (OR = 0.92, p <10−16)"
  where: Sec 3.1, p.6
- Claim: Which personas are used does not matter, nor does group diversity. What matters is that personas are present, as anchors for differentiation.
  number: persona-dummy F-test on performance, F = 1.217, p = 0.239; diversity effect on performance β = 0.067, p = 0.403
  setup: 20 personas generated once, 10 sampled per group
  quote: "what matters is the presence of personas overall—markers that allow the LLM agents to center their differentiation on—rather than who those personas are specifically."
  where: A.14, p.24
- Claim: Differentiation is not only heterogeneous learning rates. It reflects stable identities.
  number: 32% of groups have significant slopes
  quote: "Heterogeneous learning rates alone cannot explain the observed emergent synergy that persist across time"
  where: A.10, p.19

LIMITS
- Authors concede these themselves:
  - It uses a single, minimalist task (a sum-guessing game with only "too high/too low" group feedback).
  - Pairwise (k=2) measures are used because of small data, so higher-order synergy is likely missed.
  - Entropy estimation is difficult.
  - Synergy and redundancy are co-dependent and endogenous with run length.
  - It does not establish team-over-solo superiority. Footnote 2: "We do not attempt to establish team-over-solo superiority on this task."
  - Synergy "should not be interpreted as implying sophisticated cognition."
- Not shown:
  - Any success-rate gain from the prompts (Fig 2a is ns).
  - Real task quality, such as code, retrieval or planning.
  - Topologies such as graphs, hierarchies or message passing. Agents never communicate and see only the group signal, so the paper says nothing about graph topology.
- Fragility:
  - The mediation result is marginal (p = 0.053).
  - ToM emergence capacity is marginal with the time-trend null (p = 0.099), and with 3 bins it was p = 0.991 under that null. ToM passes only under the stricter functional null (p = 0.025).
  - Only 3.5% of individual groups are significant on the practical criterion.
  - The main-model Plain, Persona and ToM success percentages are not stated in the text (the Fig 2a axis tops out at 60%).
- Dated: models are GPT-4.1, Llama-3.1, Gemini 2.0 Flash and Qwen3-235B (2025 versions).

BUILDS ON
- Goldstone et al. 2024: the "group binary search" task, run with human groups.
- Rosas et al. 2020 and Mediano et al. 2022a/b, 2025: dynamical emergence and the practical criterion.
- Williams & Beer 2010: partial information decomposition (PID).
- Luppi et al. 2022, 2024: time-delayed mutual information (TDMI) and the differentiation/integration framework.
- Hausser & Strimmer 2009, Jeffreys 1946, Miller 1955: entropy estimators.
- Imai et al. 2010: causal mediation analysis.
- Chen et al. 2024: persona design.
- Deming 2022: social skills as the human-capital analogue for the ToM prompt.
- Human collective intelligence: Riedl et al. 2021, DeChurch & Mesmer-Magnus 2010, Theiner 2018.
- Multi-agent systems the paper critiques: Chen et al. 2023 (AgentVerse), Qian et al. 2023 (ChatDev-style roles), Wu et al. 2023 (AutoGen), Park et al. 2023 (generative agents).
- Related: Piedrahita et al. 2025; Cemri et al. 2025 (why multi-agent LLM systems fail).

CODE: None. The prompts are in A.1 (p.16-17). The ToM prompt adds "carefully think through step-by-step what others might guess... Consider what roles other agents might be playing (e.g., guessing higher or lower) and adapt your own adjustment to complement the group."

FIGURES
- Fig 3, p.8: "a) ToM-prompt condition has substantially more groups with significant I3 content (above 0). b) Total Stability... c) Information gain of triads over most informative dyad (G3)... d) Agent differentiation using hierarchical mixed model comparison." Best candidate: it shows the three conditions diverging on stability and differentiation while success (Fig 2a) does not.
- Alternative: Fig 1a, p.3, the differentiation / independent-complementary / integration framework diagram.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. The extraction is clean. Some minor symbol garbling in equations and inline p-values (for example "10 −16"). The extraction missed Fig 2a's exact success percentages.
